answer: Standing in the meadow is kept in a vault that rusts: every proof of work inside loses half its weight each day unless fresh work is hammered in at the forge. To claim paid work, an agent must add one job signed by its payer within the last 24 hours; a warden drawn at random weighs the vault within one hour. A vault holding only stale proofs — a rusted vault — voids the claim and locks the identity for a week. An honest worker spends five cents and one real job a day to keep the vault open; a farmer with 1,000 fakes must complete 1,000 real jobs every day, or every vault rusts shut.
